subject: maths
title: Area, Perimeter and Volume
seo_title: Year 6 Area, Perimeter and Volume Worksheets: Triangles, Parallelograms and Cuboids
standard_text: Recognise that shapes with the same areas can have different perimeters and vice versa; recognise when it is possible to use formulae for area and volume of shapes; calculate the area of parallelograms and triangles; calculate, estimate and compare volume of cubes and cuboids using standard units, including cubic centimetres (cm³) and cubic metres (m³), and extending to other units [for example, mm³ and km³].
meta_desc: Free Year 6 area, perimeter and volume worksheets for the National Curriculum: compound shapes, same area and different perimeter, area of triangles and parallelograms, volume of cubes and cuboids in cm³ and m³, and SATs-style word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Triangle: ½ × base × height. Parallelogram: base × height. Cuboid: length × width × height.
key_sub: Always use the perpendicular height, never a slanted side. Area is in square units (cm², m²); volume is in cubic units (cm³, m³). Shapes with the same area can have different perimeters.
body_html:
Area, perimeter and volume

Perimeter is the distance all the way round a shape (cm, m). Area is the flat space inside it (cm², m²). Volume is the space inside a 3-D shape (cm³, m³).

Rectangles and compound shapes

Area of a rectangle = length × width. For a compound (rectilinear) shape, split it into rectangles and add the areas. For the perimeter, find any missing lengths first, then add every side.

Same area, different perimeter. 8 cm by 3 cm and 6 cm by 4 cm both have an area of 24 cm², but their perimeters are 22 cm and 20 cm. It works the other way round too: shapes with the same perimeter can have different areas.

Triangles: area = 12 × base × perpendicular height

A triangle is half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and height. The perpendicular height meets the base at a right angle. It is the dashed line, not a slanted side.

In an obtuse-angled triangle the height can be outside the triangle. Extend the base and measure to that line.

Parallelograms: area = base × perpendicular height

Cut the triangle off one end and slide it to the other end. You get a rectangle with the same base and height.

Volume of cubes and cuboids: length × width × height

Volume counts the 1 cm cubes that fill a shape. Count the cubes in one layer, then multiply by the number of layers.

Missing length

A cuboid has a volume of 120 cm³. It is 5 cm long and 4 cm wide. How high is it?

5 × 4 × ? = 120, so 20 × ? = 120. 120 ÷ 20 = 6.

Answer: 6 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Triangle: 14 × 12 = 168 cm²Halve it: 12 × 14 × 12 = 84 cm²
Using the slanted side as the heightUse the perpendicular height (the dashed line)
Volume: 6 + 4 + 5 = 15Multiply: 6 × 4 × 5 = 120 cm³
Writing cm² for a volumeArea is cm², volume is cm³
Missing a side of a compound shapeFind the missing lengths, then add all the sides
Thinking the same area means the same perimeterWork out both: 8 cm by 3 cm and 6 cm by 4 cm have different perimeters

faq.q: How do you find the area of a triangle in Year 6?
faq.a: Multiply the base by the perpendicular height and halve it: area = ½ × base × height. For a base of 14 cm and a height of 12 cm, the area is ½ × 168 = 84 cm².

faq.q: What is the formula for the volume of a cuboid?
faq.a: Volume = length × width × height. A cuboid 6 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm has a volume of 120 cm³, which is 120 centimetre cubes.

faq.q: Is area and volume in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. The reasoning papers often ask for the area of triangles, parallelograms or compound shapes and the volume of cuboids. There is no formula sheet, so pupils need to know the formulae.

faq.q: Can two shapes have the same area but different perimeters?
faq.a: Yes. A rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm and one 6 cm by 4 cm both have an area of 24 cm², but their perimeters are 22 cm and 20 cm.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (30 cm), not the area.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 14 × 5 = 70 m². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (38 m), not the area.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96 cm². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (40 cm), not the area.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 15 × 7 = 105 m². Adding the sides gives the perimeter (44 m), not the area.

items.q: The dashed line splits the shape into two rectangles. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 4 × 7 = 28 and 6 × 3 = 18. Add: 28 + 18 = 46 cm². Use each part once: 4 × 7 + 10 × 3 = 58 counts the 4 × 3 corner twice.

items.q: The dashed line splits the shape into two rectangles. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 8 × 4 = 32. Add: 42 + 32 = 74 m². Use each part once: 6 × 7 + 14 × 4 = 98 counts the 6 × 4 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape?
items.e: Whole rectangle 13 × 9 = 117, take away the missing corner 6 × 4 = 24: 117 − 24 = 93 cm². Or: split it into two rectangles: 7 × 9 = 63 and 6 × 5 = 30. Add: 63 + 30 = 93 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape?
items.e: Whole rectangle 9 × 7 = 63, take away the missing corner 4 × 4 = 16: 63 − 16 = 47 m². Or: split it into two rectangles: 5 × 7 = 35 and 4 × 3 = 12. Add: 35 + 12 = 47 m².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape? Find the two missing lengths first.
items.e: Missing lengths: 16 − 9 = 7 and 11 − 6 = 5. Whole rectangle 16 × 11 = 176, take away the missing corner 7 × 5 = 35: 176 − 35 = 141 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape? Find the two missing lengths first.
items.e: Missing lengths: 16 − 7 = 9 and 9 − 5 = 4. Whole rectangle 16 × 9 = 144, take away the missing corner 9 × 4 = 36: 144 − 36 = 108 m².

items.q: What is the perimeter of this compound shape?
items.e: Find the missing lengths: 8 − 5 = 3 and 13 − 8 = 5. Then add all 6 sides: 8 + 3 + 5 + 5 + 13 + 8 = 42 m.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this compound shape?
items.e: Find the missing lengths: 6 + 7 = 13 and 4 + 3 = 7. Then add all 6 sides: 6 + 4 + 7 + 3 + 13 + 7 = 40 cm.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this compound shape?
items.e: Find the missing lengths: 14 − 8 = 6 and 10 − 6 = 4. Then add all 6 sides: 8 + 6 + 6 + 4 + 14 + 10 = 48 m.

items.q: Which statement about rectangles A and B is true?
items.e: Area A = 8 × 3 = 24 cm², area B = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². Perimeter A = 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 cm, perimeter B = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. Same area, different perimeters.

items.q: Which statement about rectangles A and B is true?
items.e: Perimeter A = 7 + 2 + 7 + 2 = 18 m, perimeter B = 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18 m. Area A = 7 × 2 = 14 m², area B = 5 × 4 = 20 m². Same perimeter, different areas.

items.q: Rectangle A is 8 cm by 3 cm. Rectangle B has the same area as A and is 6 cm long. What is the perimeter of rectangle B?
items.e: Area of A = 8 × 3 = 24 cm². B: 6 × ? = 24, so B is 4 cm wide. Perimeter of B = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. Same area does not mean the same perimeter (A has 22 cm).

items.q: Which rectangle has an area of 24 cm² and a perimeter of 20 cm?
items.e: 6 × 4 = 24 cm² and 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. 8 cm by 3 cm has a 22 cm perimeter, 12 cm by 2 cm has 28 cm, and 5 cm by 5 cm has the right perimeter but an area of 25 cm².

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

items.q: A square has an area of 64 m². What is its perimeter?
items.e: 8 × 8 = 64, so each side is 8 m. Perimeter = 4 × 8 = 32 m.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 cm². It is 9 cm long. How wide is it?
items.e: Length × width = area, so 9 × ? = 72. 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm. Check: 9 × 8 = 72.

items.q: What is the area of the right-angled triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the perpendicular height. Area = 12 × 12 × 16 = 12 × 192 = 96 cm². The 20 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right-angled triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the perpendicular height. Area = 12 × 9 × 12 = 12 × 108 = 54 m².

items.q: What is the area of the right-angled triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the perpendicular height. Area = 12 × 21 × 20 = 12 × 420 = 210 mm². The 29 mm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right-angled triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the perpendicular height. Area = 12 × 4 × 9 = 12 × 36 = 18 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 16 × 6 = 12 × 96 = 48 m². The 10 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 19 × 12 = 12 × 228 = 114 mm². The 37 mm side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it and meets the grey dashed line that extends the base.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 21 × 18 = 12 × 378 = 189 cm². The 19.5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 14 × 24 = 12 × 336 = 168 cm². The 40 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it and meets the grey dashed line that extends the base.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 15 × 10 = 12 × 150 = 75 m². The 12.5 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 7 × 12 = 12 × 84 = 42 mm². The 20 mm side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it and meets the grey dashed line that extends the base.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 6 × 4 = 12 × 24 = 12 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 25 × 24 = 12 × 600 = 300 cm². The 40 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it and meets the grey dashed line that extends the base.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 7.5 m and a perpendicular height of 4 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 12 × 7.5 × 4 = 12 × 30 = 15 m².

items.q: A triangle has a base of 12 cm and a perpendicular height of 6.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 12 × 12 × 6.5 = 12 × 78 = 39 cm².

items.q: A triangle has a base of 9 mm and a perpendicular height of 5 mm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 12 × 9 × 5 = 12 × 45 = 22.5 mm².

items.q: A triangle has a base of 14 cm and a perpendicular height of 11 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 12 × 14 × 11 = 12 × 154 = 77 cm².

items.q: A triangle has an area of 36 cm². Its base is 9 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
items.e: 12 × 9 × ? = 36. Double the area first: 36 × 2 = 72. Then 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm. Check: 12 × 9 × 8 = 12 × 72 = 36 cm².

items.q: A triangle has an area of 42 m². Its perpendicular height is 7 m. What is its base?
items.e: 12 × 7 × ? = 42. Double the area first: 42 × 2 = 84. Then 84 ÷ 7 = 12 m. Check: 12 × 7 × 12 = 12 × 84 = 42 m².

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 12 m and the perpendicular height is the dashed 15 m line. Area = 12 × 12 × 15 = 90 m². 12 × 15 forgets to halve, and 25 m is a slanted side.

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 21 cm and the perpendicular height is the dashed 12 cm line. Area = 12 × 21 × 12 = 126 cm². 21 × 12 forgets to halve, and 13 cm is a slanted side.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 12 × 6 = 72 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 cm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get a 12 by 6 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 14 × 8 = 112 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 m side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get a 14 by 8 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 15 × 12 = 180 mm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 13 mm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get a 15 by 12 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 16 × 9 = 144 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 15 cm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get a 16 by 9 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 16 × 15 = 240 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 17 cm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get a 16 by 15 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 8 × 4 = 32 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 m side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get an 8 by 4 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 18 × 16 = 288 mm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 20 mm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get an 18 by 16 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 8 × 3 = 24 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 cm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get an 8 by 3 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 14 × 12 = 168 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 15 cm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get a 14 by 12 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 18 × 6 = 108 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 m side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get an 18 by 6 rectangle.)

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 8.5 m and a perpendicular height of 6 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 8.5 × 6 = 51 m². Do not halve: that is only for triangles.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 14 cm and a perpendicular height of 11.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 14 × 11.5 = 161 cm². Do not halve: that is only for triangles.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 9 cm, a slanted side of 8 cm and a perpendicular height of 7 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 9 × 7 = 63 cm². The slanted 8 cm side is not used.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 96 m². Its base is 12 m. What is its perpendicular height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8 m. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 63 cm². Its perpendicular height is 7 cm. How long is its base?
A parallelogram has an area of 45 cm². Its base is 6 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
items.e: 6 × ? = 45. 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5 cm. Check: 6 × 7.5 = 45. (3.75 cm would be halving, as for a triangle.)

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Base × perpendicular height: 14 × 12 = 168 m². The 13 m side is slanted, and a parallelogram is not halved.

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Base × perpendicular height: 9 × 4 = 36 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, and a parallelogram is not halved.

items.q: A triangle and a parallelogram both have a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. How much greater is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Parallelogram: 10 × 6 = 60 cm². Triangle: 12 × 10 × 6 = 12 × 60 = 30 cm². Difference: 60 − 30 = 30 cm².

items.q: Triangle A has a base of 12 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. Parallelogram B has a base of 6 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. Which is true?
c: A is twice the area of B.
items.e: A: 12 × 12 × 8 = 12 × 96 = 48 cm². B: 6 × 8 = 48 cm². They have the same area. (Forgetting to halve makes A look twice as big.)

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 3 cubes = 6 cubes. There are 2 layers: 6 × 2 = 12 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 10 cubes can be seen).

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 5 cubes = 15 cubes. There are 3 layers: 15 × 3 = 45 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 29 cubes can be seen).

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 4 cubes = 12 cubes. There are 3 layers: 12 × 3 = 36 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 24 cubes can be seen).

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 5 cubes = 15 cubes. There are 2 layers: 15 × 2 = 30 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 22 cubes can be seen).

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 5 cubes = 10 cubes. There are 4 layers: 10 × 4 = 40 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 28 cubes can be seen).

items.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 13 × 4 × 6 = 52 × 6 = 312 cm³. Multiply all three lengths, and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 14 × 4 × 10 = 56 × 10 = 560 m³. Multiply all three lengths, and write the answer in cubic units (m³).

items.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 6 × 3 × 8 = 18 × 8 = 144 mm³. Multiply all three lengths, and write the answer in cubic units (mm³).

items.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 5 × 2 × 9 = 10 × 9 = 90 cm³. Multiply all three lengths, and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 11 × 2 × 6 = 22 × 6 = 132 m³. Multiply all three lengths, and write the answer in cubic units (m³).

items.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 14 × 6 × 8 = 84 × 8 = 672 mm³. Multiply all three lengths, and write the answer in cubic units (mm³).

items.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 10 × 4 × 6 = 40 × 6 = 240 cm³. Multiply all three lengths, and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: A cube has edges of 6 cm. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 6 cm, so volume = 6 × 6 × 6 = 36 × 6 = 216 cm³.

items.q: A cube has edges of 9 m. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 9 m, so volume = 9 × 9 × 9 = 81 × 9 = 729 m³.

items.q: The volume of this cuboid is 462 cm³. What is the missing length, marked with a question mark?
The volume of this cuboid is 120 m³. What is the missing length, marked with a question mark?
A cuboid has a volume of 288 cm³. It is 9 cm long and 8 cm tall. How wide is it?
A cuboid has a volume of 160 m³. It is 10 m long and 2 m wide. How tall is it?
Which of these would be measured in cubic metres (m³)?
c: the area of a football pitch
the water in a swimming pool
items.e: m³ measures volume, the space inside a 3-D shape, such as the water in a pool. Area is in m², length is in m and mass is in kg or tonnes.

items.q: How many cubic millimetres (mm³) are there in 1 cm³?
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so a 1 cm cube is 10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm = 1,000 mm³.

items.q: Charlie's rectangular garden is 12 m long and 9 m wide. A patio 4 m by 3 m is in one corner. The rest is lawn. What is the area of the lawn?
items.e: Garden: 12 × 9 = 108 m². Patio: 4 × 3 = 12 m². Lawn: 108 − 12 = 96 m².

items.q: Zara is laying turf on a lawn 8 m long and 6 m wide. Turf costs £4 per m². How much does the turf cost?
items.e: Area: 8 × 6 = 48 m². Cost: 48 × £4 = £192. (£112 uses the perimeter, 28 m, instead of the area.)

items.q: A lawn is 8 m long and 6 m wide. How much fencing is needed to go all the way round it?
items.e: All the way round is the perimeter: 8 + 6 + 8 + 6 = 28 m. 48 is the area, and 14 m is only two sides.

items.q: Oliver has 24 square paving slabs, each 1 m by 1 m. He uses all of them to make a rectangular patio. Which patio has the shortest perimeter?
items.e: All four have an area of 24 m². Perimeters: 6 m by 4 m = 20 m, 8 m by 3 m = 22 m, 12 m by 2 m = 28 m, 24 m by 1 m = 50 m. The closer to a square, the shorter the perimeter.

items.q: Grace has 20 m of fencing for a rectangular rabbit run. Which run gives the rabbits the most space?
items.e: Every run has a perimeter of 20 m. Areas: 5 × 5 = 25 m², 6 × 4 = 24 m², 7 × 3 = 21 m², 8 × 2 = 16 m². Same perimeter, different areas.

items.q: Ava paints a wall 5 m wide and 2.4 m high. There is a door in the wall 2 m high and 0.9 m wide. What area does she paint?
Two walls are each 5 m wide and 2.6 m high. One tin of paint covers 10 m². How many tins are needed to paint both walls?
items.e: One wall: 5 × 2.6 = 13 m². Two walls: 26 m². 26 ÷ 10 = 2.6, so 2 tins are not enough: round up to 3 tins.

items.q: A triangular flower bed has a base of 6 m and a perpendicular height of 3.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 12 × 6 × 3.5 = 12 × 21 = 10.5 m².

items.q: Alfie makes bunting from 20 triangular flags. Each flag has a base of 15 cm and a perpendicular height of 20 cm. How much fabric do the flags use altogether?
items.e: One flag: 12 × 15 × 20 = 12 × 300 = 150 cm². 20 flags: 20 × 150 = 3,000 cm².

items.q: A flower bed is a parallelogram. Its base is 5 m, its slanted sides are 3 m, and its perpendicular height is 2.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 5 × 2.5 = 12.5 m². The 3 m sides are slanted, so they are not used.

items.q: A fish tank is a cuboid 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: Volume = 60 × 30 × 40 = 1,800 × 40 = 72,000 cm³. 1,800 is only the area of the base.

items.q: Amelia's fish tank is 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre. How many litres of water does the tank hold when it is full?
A fish tank is 40 cm long, 20 cm wide and 40 cm high. It is filled with water to a depth of 25 cm. How many litres of water are in the tank? (1,000 cm³ = 1 litre)
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 40 × 20 × 25 = 20,000 cm³. 20,000 ÷ 1,000 = 20 litres. (32 litres is the full tank.)

items.q: A box of sugar cubes is 8 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm high. Each sugar cube is 1 cm³. How many sugar cubes fill the box?
items.e: One layer: 8 × 5 = 40 cubes. 3 layers: 40 × 3 = 120 sugar cubes.

items.q: Noah packs sugar cubes with 2 cm edges into a box 10 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm high. How many sugar cubes fit?
items.e: Along each edge: 10 ÷ 2 = 5, 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Cubes: 5 × 3 × 2 = 30. (240 would be 1 cm cubes.)

items.q: A sandpit is 2 m long and 1.5 m wide. It is filled with sand 0.2 m deep. What volume of sand is needed?
items.e: Volume = 2 × 1.5 × 0.2 = 3 × 0.2 = 0.6 m³. 3 m² is only the area of the sandpit.

items.q: A box is a cube with 1 m edges. How many 1 cm cubes would fill it?
A box has a volume of 480 cm³. Its base is 12 cm by 8 cm. How high is the box?
items.e: Area of base: 12 × 8 = 96 cm². 96 × ? = 480, so the height is 480 ÷ 96 = 5 cm. Check: 12 × 8 × 5 = 480.

items.q: A swimming pool is 25 m long and 10 m wide. The water is 2 m deep everywhere. What is the volume of the water?
items.e: Volume = 25 × 10 × 2 = 250 × 2 = 500 m³. 250 m² is only the area of the pool.

items.q: Box A is a cube with 10 cm edges. Box B is 20 cm by 5 cm by 8 cm. Which box has the greater volume, and by how much?
items.e: A: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000 cm³. B: 20 × 5 × 8 = 800 cm³. A is greater by 1,000 − 800 = 200 cm³. (Adding the edges gives 30 and 33, but that is not volume.)
